draft.title: Muscle fibre types
card: fibres contract slowly and resist fatigue. They use oxygen well to keep working for a long time, so they suit endurance activities.
fibres contract quickly and with great force, but they tire fast. They suit short, powerful efforts.
Every muscle holds a mix of both types. The mix differs between people, and training can change how well each type performs.
An activity that needs long, steady effort relies more on slow-twitch fibres. An activity that needs a burst of force relies more on fast-twitch fibres.
draft.remember: Slow-twitch fibres last. Fast-twitch fibres give force and speed but tire fast.

a.q: Which description best fits fast-twitch muscle fibres?
opts: They give quick, forceful contractions but tire fast
They give slow, gentle contractions and tire fast
They give quick, forceful contractions and resist fatigue
They give slow, gentle contractions and resist fatigue
a.why: Fast-twitch fibres contract quickly and powerfully, but they tire fast. The option with quick contractions and resistance to fatigue describes a mix of both types and fits neither.
a.clue: Think of the fibres used in a short burst of force.

b.q: Priya runs a 10 km race through the hills near Bathurst at a steady pace. Which fibres does she rely on most?
opts: Slow-twitch fibres, because they resist fatigue
Fast-twitch fibres, because they contract with great force
Slow-twitch fibres, because they contract quickly
Fast-twitch fibres, because they resist fatigue
b.why: A long, steady effort needs fibres that keep working without tiring, and that is what slow-twitch fibres do. Fast-twitch fibres give great force, but they tire fast, so they are not suited to a long race.
b.clue: Which fibres keep working for a long time?

a.best: They give quick, forceful contractions but tire fast

b.best: Slow-twitch fibres, because they resist fatigue
